title: spec review: S3b stale-work severity and critical-path aware steering in shadow: low continue, medium steer with changed evidence, high cancel or hold, critical-path workers first (P28, P29)
spec:
orchestrator/stale.py evidence(): add severity (none|low|medium|high) and severity_reasons: high when a moved path is in the task's write scope or is a test named in its acceptance; medium when a moved path is in its read scope or imported by a file in its write scope (use the existing repo links when available); low otherwise; none when nothing moved. orchestrator/steering_policy.py: new trigger stale_severity evaluated before dependency_changed: low continue; medium steer with a message listing the moved paths and the goal head sha; high cancel when the task has not yet committed anything in its worktree, else steer plus hold_after_gate flag (the daemon holds the task after its next gate for the Planner with hold_reason stale_high) — never auto-rebase silently for high. Critical path: daemon evaluates running tasks in critical_path.rank order and, when [steering].noncritical_medium_continue is true (default true, dated comment), a medium severity on a task not on the critical path is continue with reason noncritical. Shadow rows kind steering carry severity, critical (bool) and the would-be action; active applies. Also record for every row the accepted-task economics fields the scorecard needs later (tokens so far from the registry, elapsed). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/12-steering-policy.md gains the severity table and the critical-path rule.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Task worktrees carry no .orchestrator runs, tasks or decision_log state: tests use synthetic fixtures; for any measured numbers in docs run read-only against /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator via an explicit root argument. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Contracts of the earlier modules: .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and docs/hermes-hardening/*.md on this branch; read the merged modules before building on them.

risks.issue: The spec says high severity cancels when nothing is committed. The daemon already downgrades every active cancel to steer (cancel_shadow_only, daemon.py ~1710). The spec does not say whether stale_severity cancel stays shadow-only or becomes live. A live cancel of a worker with uncommitted dirty edits is a deletion-like action that needs approval. no_commits() only compares HEAD to the merge-base, so it says nothing about a dirty worktree.

hold_after_gate has no existing mechanism. The spec gives no storage location for the flag (a pipeline key?), no clearing rule, and no rule for setting it only in effective active mode. The steering loop downgrades to shadow when promotion is refused, so the flag must never be written then. The hold has to be applied in the gate stage (~1340-1375), which currently auto-rebases and holds on stale_rebase_conflict (~1301). That is the silent-rebase path the spec forbids for high, and the spec does not name it. hold_reason stale_high also needs handling in the held-task release/resume logic (~151-167), or it will be treated as an unknown reason or auto-released.

evidence_hash hashes result['evidence']. Adding tokens-so-far and elapsed to that dict changes the hash every tick. That defeats the dedupe and writes a steering row per running task per tick. The economics fields must go in extra only, and stay out of the hash. The spec should also say which registry field supplies tokens. If that field is missing, the value should be null rather than 0.

The spec does not cover the git-failure path. _unknown() returns risk 'unknown', and the severity enum has no matching value. Defaulting to none or low would be a silent fallback. Specify severity 'unknown' with a reason, and make sure steering treats it as continue. STALE_KEYS is a required-key check, so adding 'severity' there would send every existing fixture and caller to missing_input. Make it optional and derive it when absent.

'Imported by a file in its write scope' and 'test named in its acceptance' have no implementation source. evidence() does not receive acceptance, and the graph links are optional and often stale. Steering's read_scope() already does the AST import walk. Importing it from stale.py would couple the two modules, so move the shared helper or say which module owns it. Acceptance ids (tests/test_x.py::name) must be parsed to a path. Define precedence: high beats medium beats low, and low for moved paths that are outside both scopes.

stale_severity overlaps the existing security_concern and dependency_changed triggers, which use the risk field and the read scope. The spec does not say how they interact. Two overlapping signals (risk and severity) can double count or contradict, for example risk high with severity low. Say which trigger wins, or that stale_severity replaces the stale part of dependency_changed. Existing tests around security_concern must stay green.

'Critical' is currently ranked[0]==task, so one task. The spec says 'not on the critical path' and 'evaluate in critical_path.rank order' without defining the set. The steering loop iterates running in bus order, not rank order. Define critical as the head of the rank, or as the whole chain that critical_path.explain reports. Reorder running by ranked position, and put durations=None (rank failure) in as a defined case: treat as critical, so medium still steers.

suggested_spec_changes: State that the stale_severity high cancel stays shadow-only, consistent with cancel_shadow_only. In active mode, high with no commits becomes a steer plus hold_after_gate, with the candidate action recorded as cancel. Or get explicit approval for a live cancel, and guard it against a dirty worktree.

Specify the hold_after_gate storage (a pipeline key on the task), where it is written (only when the effective mode is active and the steer applied), and where it is consumed (the gate stage, before any auto-rebase). Cover clearing it on release and on merge, and how hold_reason stale_high is handled in the held-task release logic.
Keep the economics fields (tokens_so_far, elapsed_s, severity, critical) in decision_log extra and out of evidence_hash. Name the registry field that supplies tokens, and use null when it is absent.
Define the severity enum including 'unknown' for git failure (steering: continue). Keep 'severity' optional in STALE_KEYS and derive it when it is absent.
Define precedence between stale_severity and the existing dependency_changed and security_concern triggers, and which module owns the shared import-walk helper.
Define the critical set and iterate running in rank order. Say what happens when ranking fails (treat as critical).

Validate noncritical_medium_continue as a bool and include tests/test_pool.py in scope if it checks pool.toml keys. Add a rollback note: set the flag to false, or set steering.mode back to shadow or off.
